items.stem:
Here is a list of numbers.

15   21   23   27   32   36   49   51

From this list, write down

parts.t: the prime number,
the cube number.

sols: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself.
15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7, 27 = 3<sup>3</sup>, 32 = 2<sup>5</sup>, 36 = 6<sup>2</sup>, 49 = 7<sup>2</sup> and 51 = 3 × 17, so all of these have a third factor.
each one splits into a product of smaller factors
23 has no factor other than 1 and 23
A cube number is an integer multiplied by itself three times.
The cube number in the list is 27.
32 is a power of 2 but 32 = 2<sup>5</sup>, which is not a cube

parts.t: Write 108 as a product of its prime factors.
Write down the square number that is a factor of 108 and is greater than 30.

ms:
M1 for a correct factor tree or repeated division reaching 2, 2, 3, 3, 3
A1 (accept 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3)
sols: Divide by prime numbers, smallest first.
The square numbers among them are 1, 4, 9 and 36.
The only one greater than 30 is 36.

parts.t: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 24 and 36.
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 24 and 36.

ms:
M1 for 23 × 32 or for listing 24, 48, 72, … and 36, 72, …
A1
sols: For the HCF take the lower power of each prime that appears in both.
For the LCM take the higher power of every prime that appears.
72 = 3 × 24 = 2 × 36, so it is a multiple of both

items.stem:
At Harbour Bus Station a bus to Marina leaves every 12 minutes and a bus to Riverside leaves every 18 minutes.
A bus to Marina and a bus to Riverside both leave the station at 08 00.

parts.t: Find the next time that a bus to Marina and a bus to Riverside leave the station at the same time.
Work out how many more times before 10 00 the two buses leave the station at the same time.

ms:
M1 for LCM(12, 18) = 36 or for listing 12, 24, 36, … and 18, 36, …
A1 cao
sols: The buses leave together after a number of minutes that is a multiple of both 12 and 18.
LCM(12, 18) = 36, so they next leave together 36 minutes after 08 00.
the lowest common multiple is the first time the two patterns meet
From 08 00 to 10 00 is 120 minutes, and 36, 72 and 108 are the multiples of 36 that are less than 120.

parts.t: Write 300 as a product of its prime factors.
Find the smallest positive integer n such that 540n is a cube number.

ms:
M1 for a correct method reaching 2, 2, 3, 5, 5
A1

M1 for identifying that one more 2 and two more 5s are needed (23 × 33 × 53)
A1 (540 × 50 = 27 000 = 303)
sols: Divide 300 by prime numbers, smallest first.
A number is a cube number exactly when every index in its prime factorisation is a multiple of 3.
The index of 2 must rise from 2 to 3, and the index of 5 from 1 to 3, so one more 2 and two more 5s are needed.
the index of 3 is already 3, a multiple of 3

parts.t: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of P and Q.
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of P and Q. Give your answer as a product of prime factors.

ms:
M1 for taking the lower power of each common prime (22, 3, 5)
A1

M1 for taking the higher power of every prime
A1 oe (12 600)
sols: For the HCF, use only the primes that appear in both, each to the lower power.
2: lower of 23 and 22 is 22.  3: lower of 32 and 31 is 3.  5: lower of 51 and 52 is 5.  7 appears in Q only, so it is not used.
For the LCM, use every prime that appears, each to the higher power.

items.stem: The Venn diagram shows the prime factors of 84 and of 90.

parts.t: Write down the highest common factor (HCF) of 84 and 90.
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 84 and 90.
Show that HCF × LCM = 84 × 90.

ms:
M1 for 2 × 7 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 oe (all six numbers in the diagram)
A1
sols: The HCF is the product of the numbers in the overlap.
these are the prime factors that 84 and 90 have in common
The LCM is the product of all the numbers in the diagram.
for any two integers, HCF × LCM equals their product

items.stem: For any two positive integers, HCF × LCM = the product of the two integers.

parts.t:
Two numbers have a highest common factor of 8 and a lowest common multiple of 120. One of the numbers is 24.
Find the other number.

Two different numbers have a highest common factor of 6 and a lowest common multiple of 90.
Neither number is 6 and neither number is 90.
Find the two numbers.

ms:
M1 for 6a and 6b with ab = 15 and a, b coprime, or for a correct trial of a pair
A1 both, cao
sols: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
960 = 24 × (the other number), so the other number = 960 ÷ 24 = 40
Both numbers are multiples of 6, so write them as 6a and 6b with a and b having no common factor.
HCF × LCM = product of the numbers
ab = 15 gives a = 1, b = 15 (the numbers 6 and 90, not allowed) or a = 3, b = 5.

items.stem:
A rectangular floor measures 4.5 m by 3.6 m.
It is to be covered completely by identical square tiles, with no gaps and no tiles cut.

parts.t: Find the largest possible length of the side of a tile. Give your answer in centimetres.
Work out the number of tiles needed.

These tiles cost $7.25 each.
Work out the total cost of the tiles.

ms:
M1 for 450 and 360 seen and an HCF method
A1 cao
sols: Work in centimetres: the floor is 450 cm by 360 cm.
A tile of side d cm fits exactly only if d divides both 450 and 360, so the largest tile has side HCF(450, 360).

parts.t: Write 1176 as a product of its prime factors.
Find the smallest positive integer m such that 1176m is a square number.
Find the smallest positive integer k such that 1176k is a cube number.

ms:
M1 for a correct method reaching 2, 2, 2, 3, 7, 7
A1

M1 for identifying that the powers of 2 and of 3 are odd, so 2 × 3 is needed
A1 (1176 × 6 = 7056 = 842)

M1 for needing 32 and 7 to make every index a multiple of 3
A1 (1176 × 63 = 74 088 = 423)
sols: A number is a square number exactly when every index in its prime factorisation is even.
In 2<sup>3</sup> × 3<sup>1</sup> × 7<sup>2</sup> the indices of 2 and of 3 are odd; the index of 7 is already even.
One more 2 and one more 3 are needed, so m = 2 × 3 = 6
A number is a cube number exactly when every index is a multiple of 3.
The index of 2 is 3 ✓; the index of 3 must rise from 1 to 3; the index of 7 must rise from 2 to 3.
